short: A tough frontier general who split administration of the empire with his brother and held the Rhine and Danube.
full:
Valentinian, an army officer from Pannonia, was chosen by senior generals and officials on 26 February 364 CE, weeks after the sudden death of Julian's short-lived successor left the throne empty. Within a month he made his brother Valens co-emperor and gave him the eastern provinces, keeping the west and its harder frontiers for himself, a division that proved durable even though the two halves were meant to remain a single empire.

Valentinian spent most of his reign campaigning in person against Germanic peoples along the Rhine and Danube, founding forts and repelling incursions including the Great Conspiracy, a coordinated assault on Roman Britain in 367 CE. He died of a stroke, reportedly brought on by rage at insolent Germanic envoys, on 17 November 375 CE, leaving the west to his young sons and founding the Valentinianic dynasty.
